title: The Rise and Fall of American Europe
gist: Andrew Moravcsik's review of Glyn Morgan's book argues the 75-year-old 'American Europe' is collapsing but criticizes its purely military, realist framing; he says economic ties in energy, tech, finance and more will be the real great-power battleground.

insights.claim: Glyn Morgan argues that the 75-year-old transatlantic order, 'American Europe', is now collapsing after the Cold War's end and the rise of the MAGA movement.
insights.speaker: Foreign Affairs
insights.so_what: A US troop drawdown from Europe is a stated baseline in this school of analysis; watch European defense spending and NATO reform.

insights.claim: Morgan treats European unification as little more than a US-conceived and US-funded project to bolster an anti-Soviet military alliance, implying that US troop withdrawal becomes inevitable once the Soviet Union is gone.
insights.speaker: Foreign Affairs
insights.so_what: Reviewer calls this extreme and idiosyncratically realist; treat as one contested view of why US commitment may fade.

insights.claim: MAGA Republicans' criticism of Europe is driven in part by ideological antipathy to Europe's welfare states and liberal values.
insights.speaker: Foreign Affairs
insights.so_what: Transatlantic friction has an ideological, not just burden-sharing, component.

insights.claim: Morgan's proposals for reforming or replacing NATO institutions look neither promising nor likely, owing to European disunity and weakness.
insights.speaker: Foreign Affairs
insights.so_what: Institutional NATO reform is unlikely to be a near-term catalyst.
insights.locator: Morgan closes with a long analysis

insights.claim: Moravcsik contends the book omits economic relations in energy, arms, high tech, entertainment, pharmaceuticals, and financial and digital services, where the EU remains active and US-European links are robust.
insights.speaker: Foreign Affairs
insights.so_what: Transatlantic decoupling is overstated if one looks at commercial ties rather than troop levels.
insights.quote: it hardly touches on economic relations in areas such as energy, arms, high tech, entertainment, pharmaceuticals, financial and digital services
insights.locator: Surprisingly for a book about twenty-first-century order

insights.claim: Economic issues rather than military defense may be the critical battleground among the United States, China and other great powers in the coming decades.
insights.speaker: Foreign Affairs
insights.so_what: Favors positioning around trade, tech and financial-services rules over pure defense-theme trades.
insights.quote: Such issues, not military defense, may well be the critical battleground
